answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A nectar delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A island check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A copper penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 3259 identities need 3259 bonds of 67 tokens, 59097 dollars of hardware and 49 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
